## formal
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a smooth gravitational field on four-dimensional flat spacetime with vanishing torsion (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $D = \hb^{T}(\partial_{a})D_{a}$ its covariant vector derivative, $\mathcal{R}$ its curvature operator, $\mathcal{R}(b) = \partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b)$ the Ricci vector and $\mathcal{R}_{0} = \partial_{a}\cdot\mathcal{R}(a)$ the scalar. Hypothesis (PI), as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.vacuum-polarisation-kernel-on-a-gravitational-field-has-the-flat-leading-part-and-no-weyl-term-of-degree-four}: the protraction identity $\partial_{a}\wedge\mathcal{R}(a\wedge b) = 0$, the first Bianchi identity of a torsion-free field (classical). For a physical vector field $A$ write
\[
K_{1}A = \nabla^{2}A, \qquad K_{2}A = D\,(D\cdot A), \qquad K_{3}A = m^{2}A, \qquad K_{4}A = \mathcal{R}_{0}\,A, \qquad K_{5}A = \mathcal{R}(A),
\]
with $\nabla^{2}A = \sum_{k} Q(\gamma_{k})\bigl[(\gamma_{k}\cdot D)(\gamma_{k}\cdot D)A - ((\gamma_{k}\cdot D)\gamma_{k})\cdot D\,A\bigr]$ the rough Laplacian on an orthonormal physical frame $\{\gamma_{k}\}$. A \emph{local term for two vector slots of degree of divergence $2$} is a kernel $(a, x; b, x') \mapsto a\cdot K_{x}\bigl(b\,\delta(x, x')\bigr)$ with $K$ a differential operator of order at most $2$ on physical vector fields of the form that Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-local-covariance-with-scaling-of-time-ordered-products}(iii) gives to the difference of two extensions that are local and covariant with almost homogeneous scaling: the coefficient of the derivatives of order $j$ is a polynomial with constant coefficients in $\mathcal{R}$, its covariant derivatives and the mass $m$, of dimension $2 - j$, covariant under the rotation gauge.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The list; proved given the form of the cited Fact and (PI), the dimensions of the invariant spaces by exact rank.)} Every such term is $K = \sum_{i=1}^{5}c_{i}K_{i}$ with real constants $c_{i}$: five constants in place of the $15$ coefficient functions of the point per index pair of clause (iv) of the cited theorem. The count: no Lorentz-invariant tensor has three vector slots, so there is no term $m\,D$; with four vector slots there are four invariants, two symmetric in the derivative pair ($K_{1}$, $K_{2}$ up to lower order) and two antisymmetric, which multiply commutators of covariant derivatives and are curvature terms without derivatives; the invariant bilinear forms in $(a, b)$ that are linear in a map of bivectors number $6$ for all maps, $3$ on symmetric maps, $2$ on maps obeying (PI), namely $a\cdot\mathcal{R}(b)$ and $(a\cdot b)\,\mathcal{R}_{0}$, and $0$ on maps that also have vanishing Ricci vector. So the Weyl part of the curvature operator cannot occur in the difference of two extensions, and no parity-odd term occurs although invariance is imposed for the connected group only.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Transversality; proved.)} On every torsion-free field, $D\wedge D\chi = 0$ for scalar fields $\chi$ and
\[
D\cdot(D\wedge A) = \nabla^{2}A - D\,(D\cdot A) + \mathcal{R}(A)
\]
in the store's sign of the curvature operator. The condition $K(D\chi) = 0$ for every scalar $\chi$, on every torsion-free field and for every mass, holds exactly when $(c_{1}, c_{2}, c_{3}, c_{4}, c_{5}) = c\,(1, -1, 0, 0, 1)$, that is
\[
K A = c\;D\cdot(D\wedge A),
\]
the divergence of the field strength of $A$. On the flat field this is $c\,(\nabla^{2}A - \nabla(\nabla\cdot A))$, the transverse term $c\,T(\delta)$ of clause (iii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants} up to the sign convention of $T$: the constant $Z_{3}$. A photon mass term ($c_{3}$) and the two curvature couplings ($c_{4}$, $c_{5}$ other than the value fixed by $c_{1}$) are excluded.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What this gives for the stored clause; proved given the two imported Facts and the hypothesis that the degree of divergence is $2$.)} Assume, as argued in clause (iv) of the cited curved-field theorem from Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products}(ii) and (vi), that the time-ordered one-loop vacuum-polarisation kernel on the field has degree of divergence $2$. Then any two extensions of it that are local and covariant with almost homogeneous scaling and transverse in one slot differ by $c\,a\cdot D\cdot(D\wedge(b\,\delta))$ with one real constant $c$, the same on every torsion-free field: the freedom is the flat $Z_{3}$, and the coefficient of the Ricci term relative to the Laplacian is fixed.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Existence of a transverse extension; argued, not proved.)} Suppose in addition that the failure of transversality of a local covariant extension, the map $\chi \mapsto \bar\Pi(D\chi)$, is itself a local term of the form of the cited Fact with dimension $3$, and that the kernel is symmetric under exchange of its two slots; neither is part of the stored Facts. The candidates are $D(D\cdot D\chi)$, $m^{2}D\chi$, $\mathcal{R}_{0}D\chi$, $\mathcal{R}(D\chi)$ and $(D\mathcal{R}_{0})\chi$. The first four are $K_{2}$ to $K_{5}$ applied to $D\chi$ and are removed by subtracting local terms of (i); the fifth gives a double divergence $\int\chi\,(D\mathcal{R}_{0})\cdot D\psi$ that is not symmetric in $(\chi, \psi)$ and is excluded by the symmetry. Under these two suppositions a transverse local covariant extension exists. What is missing in the store is a statement that the divergence of a local covariant time-ordered product of currents is of this local form (the literature's Ward identity or principle of perturbative agreement on a gravitational field).
\end{enumerate}

## technical
The stored curved-field result found that, at each point, the vacuum polarisation on a gravitational field has the same fifteen undetermined local terms per pair of indices as on flat spacetime, but with coefficients that could vary from point to point, and it cited the imported local-covariance Fact for their reduction to constants without carrying the reduction out. This result carries it out. The Fact says each coefficient is a constant-coefficient polynomial in the curvature operator, its derivatives and the mass, of a fixed dimension, and the construction is covariant under local rotations; so each coefficient is a Lorentz-invariant tensor, and the invariant tensors can be counted exactly as the common kernel of the Lorentz generators acting through the algebra. With two derivatives there are two terms, the rough Laplacian and the gradient of the divergence; with one derivative none, because no invariant has three vector slots; with no derivative the mass squared, and two terms linear in the curvature, the Ricci map and the scalar curvature, the Weyl part admitting no invariant. The count of curvature terms uses the protraction identity: on symmetric maps without it there is a third invariant. That is five constants. Requiring that two extensions both obey the Ward identity makes their difference annihilate gradients. For a torsion-free field the curl of a gradient vanishes and the divergence of the field strength equals the Laplacian minus the gradient of the divergence plus the Ricci map, in the store's sign; an exact computation on a sample field shows the four other directions fail independently, so the transverse terms are the multiples of the divergence of the field strength. Given the imported Facts and the flat degree of divergence, two transverse local covariant extensions therefore differ by the one constant of flat spacetime. Whether a transverse local covariant extension exists on a gravitational field is not proved here; it is argued under two further suppositions that the store does not hold.

## lay
The effect by which a photon briefly becomes an electron and positron pair has an infinite part that a rule must fix, and the rule leaves some quantities free. On flat spacetime the free quantities reduce to one number, which is absorbed into the measured electric charge. On a gravitational field the collection had shown only that the free quantities are of the same kind at each point, and had relied on a theorem from the literature, taken as an imported fact and quoted from memory, to say they are the same everywhere. This result works out what that theorem leaves, assuming it and assuming gravity without the twisting that spinning matter would source. The answer is five numbers: two that already exist on flat spacetime, a possible photon mass, and two couplings of the photon to curvature. Demanding that electric charge be conserved, for both of two competing rules, removes four of them. What remains is the single number of flat spacetime, and the coupling to curvature comes with a fixed strength instead of a free one. The tidal part of gravity, the only part present in empty space, cannot appear among the free quantities at all. The result does not show that a charge-conserving rule exists on a gravitational field; that is argued under extra assumptions and is known in the literature, not derived here.

## one-liner
Given the imported local-covariance Fact, the protraction identity and degree of divergence $2$, on a torsion-free gravitational field two local covariant extensions of the one-loop vacuum polarisation differ by $c_{1}\nabla^{2} + c_{2}D(D\cdot) + c_{3}m^{2} + c_{4}\mathcal{R}_{0} + c_{5}\mathcal{R}(\cdot)$ (five constants, no Weyl term), and if both are transverse by $c\,D\cdot(D\wedge A) = c\,(\nabla^{2}A - D(D\cdot A) + \mathcal{R}(A))$, the flat constant $Z_{3}$ (proved); existence of a transverse extension is argued only.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\begin{proof}
\emph{(i).} By Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-local-covariance-with-scaling-of-time-ordered-products}(iii) with $\omega = 2$, the coefficient of the derivatives of order $j$ in $K$ is a polynomial with constant coefficients in $\mathcal{R}$, its covariant derivatives and $m$, of dimension $2 - j$, where $\mathcal{R}$ has dimension $2$ and each covariant derivative and $m$ dimension $1$. The construction is covariant under the rotation gauge (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}(e)), under which the slot vectors $a$, $b$, the derivative directions and $\mathcal{R}$ rotate together and the constants do not change; so each coefficient is a multilinear function of its vector slots, and of $\mathcal{R}$ where it occurs, invariant under rotors, hence annihilated by the action of every bivector $J$, $v \mapsto J\times v$ on vectors and $M \mapsto J\times M(\cdot) - M(J\times\cdot)$ on maps of bivectors. The bivectors $\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$, $\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ generate the Lorentz algebra under the commutator product, so invariance under these three suffices; the check computes the dimension of each invariant space as the corank of the three generators acting on the tensor product, exactly.

\emph{Order $2$:} dimension $0$, so the coefficient is an invariant of four vector slots $(a, b; u, v)$, $u, v$ the derivative directions. The space has dimension $4$; the part symmetric in $(u, v)$ has dimension $2$, spanned by $(a\cdot b)(u\cdot v)$ and $(a\cdot u)(b\cdot v) + (a\cdot v)(b\cdot u)$, which give $K_{1}$ and $K_{2}$ up to the order of the derivatives; the antisymmetric part has dimension $2$ and multiplies $[u\cdot D, v\cdot D]$, which on a torsion-free field is the action of the field strength, a term of order $0$ linear in $\mathcal{R}$. Changing the order of two covariant derivatives in $K_{1}$ or $K_{2}$ likewise adds terms of order $0$ linear in $\mathcal{R}$, and of order $1$ none, the torsion being zero. \emph{Order $1$:} dimension $1$; the only quantity of dimension $1$ is $m$, and the coefficient would be $m$ times an invariant of three vector slots, of which there is none. \emph{Order $0$:} dimension $2$: $m^{2}$ times the one invariant $a\cdot b$ of two vector slots, giving $K_{3}$, and terms linear in $\mathcal{R}$; derivatives of $\mathcal{R}$ have dimension at least $3$. The bilinear forms in $(a, b)$ linear in a map $M$ of bivectors and invariant form a space of dimension $6$; on symmetric maps $3$; on the maps with $\partial_{a}\wedge M(a\wedge c) = 0$, where $\mathcal{R}$ lies by (PI), dimension $2$. The forms $a\cdot M(b)$ and $(a\cdot b)\,\partial_{c}\cdot M(c)$ are invariant and are independent (the check evaluates them on a map of Ricci type), so they span, giving $K_{5}$ and $K_{4}$. On the maps that in addition have $\partial_{a}\cdot M(a\wedge c) = 0$ the dimension is $0$. The identification of maps with tensors in the check uses the invariant form $\langle AB\rangle_{0}$ on bivectors, which is nondegenerate, so the space of invariant forms on a subspace of maps has the dimension of the invariant tensors in that subspace times the two vector slots. This gives the list. The invariance used is that of the connected group; a parity-odd term would appear as an invariant in these counts and none survives.

\emph{(ii).} For a scalar $\chi$, $D\chi = g^{\mu}\partial_{\mu}\chi$ with $g^{\mu} = \hb^{T}(e^{\mu})$, and $D\wedge D\chi = (D\wedge g^{\mu})\,\partial_{\mu}\chi + g^{\nu}\wedge g^{\mu}\,\partial_{\nu}\partial_{\mu}\chi = 0$, the first term by the torsion equation of the definition, clause (f), the second by symmetry. The identity $D\cdot(D\wedge A) = \nabla^{2}A - D(D\cdot A) + \mathcal{R}(A)$ is the classical Weitzenb\"ock formula for vector fields; in the store's conventions it reads as follows. Both sides are covariant under the rotation gauge, so fix a point and a gauge with $\Omega = 0$ there. Write $D_{k} = \gamma_{k}\cdot D = D_{\hb(\gamma_{k})}$ for an orthonormal physical frame $\{\gamma_{k}\}$ of constant vectors, so that $D = \gamma^{k}D_{k}$ and $D_{k}\gamma_{l} = \Omega(\hb(\gamma_{k}))\times\gamma_{l} = 0$ at the point. There
\[
D\cdot(D\wedge A) = \sum_{k,l}\gamma^{k}\cdot\bigl(\gamma^{l}\wedge D_{k}D_{l}A\bigr) = \sum_{k,l}\bigl[(\gamma^{k}\cdot\gamma^{l})\,D_{k}D_{l}A - \gamma^{l}\,\bigl(\gamma^{k}\cdot D_{k}D_{l}A\bigr)\bigr] .
\]
The first sum is $\sum_{k}Q(\gamma_{k})D_{k}D_{k}A$, which is $\nabla^{2}A$ at the point, the correction term $((\gamma_{k}\cdot D)\gamma_{k})\cdot D A$ of the rough Laplacian vanishing there. In the second, $D_{k}D_{l} = D_{l}D_{k} + [D_{k}, D_{l}]$; $\sum_{k}\gamma^{k}\cdot D_{l}D_{k}A = D_{l}(D\cdot A)$ at the point, so that part is $-D(D\cdot A)$. The commutator of the derivatives along the background vector fields $\hb(\gamma_{k})$, $\hb(\gamma_{l})$ is the field strength on their plane plus the derivative along their Lie bracket, whose physical image is $D_{k}\gamma_{l} - D_{l}\gamma_{k}$ by the torsion equation and vanishes at the point; so by clause (c) of the definition $[D_{k}, D_{l}]A = R(\hb(\gamma_{k}\wedge\gamma_{l}))\times A = -\mathcal{R}(\gamma_{k}\wedge\gamma_{l})\cdot A$. With $(B\cdot A)\cdot c = -(B\cdot c)\cdot A$ for a bivector $B$, $\gamma^{k}\cdot\bigl(\mathcal{R}(\gamma_{k}\wedge\gamma_{l})\cdot A\bigr) = \bigl(\gamma^{k}\cdot\mathcal{R}(\gamma_{k}\wedge\gamma_{l})\bigr)\cdot A = \mathcal{R}(\gamma_{l})\cdot A$, and the remaining term is $+\sum_{l}\gamma^{l}\,(\mathcal{R}(\gamma_{l})\cdot A) = \mathcal{R}(A)$, the Ricci map being symmetric under (PI). The sign of this term is the point of convention; the check verifies the identity exactly on a torsion-free polynomial field with a generic vector field, in the store's sign and not the opposite one, with the library whose curvature sign is that of the definition. Hence $K(D\chi) = 0$ for $K = c\,(K_{1} - K_{2} + K_{5})$, on every torsion-free field.

Conversely let $K = \sum c_{i}K_{i}$ with $K(D\chi) = 0$ for all $\chi$, all torsion-free fields and all masses. The constants do not depend on the field or the mass, so the conditions from any one field and any values of the mass are necessary. The check evaluates $K_{i}(D\chi)$ at a point of one polynomial torsion-free field, with its curvature jet exact, for two cubic scalars $\chi$ and two values of $m^{2}$: the resulting linear system in $(c_{1}, \dots, c_{5})$ has rank $4$ and its solutions are the multiples of $(1, -1, 0, 0, 1)$. With the first half this proves the statement. On the flat field $\mathcal{R} = 0$ and $D = \nabla$, so $K A = c\,(\nabla^{2}A - \nabla(\nabla\cdot A))$; contracted with $a$ and applied to $b\,\delta$ this is $-c\,a\cdot T(\delta)(b)$ with $T(f)(a) = (a\cdot\nabla)\nabla f - a\nabla^{2}f$ the transverse operator of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}, whose clause (iii) finds the transverse differences of degree at most $2$ to be the multiples of this term.

\emph{(iii).} The hypothesis is the degree of divergence $2$ that clause (iv) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.vacuum-polarisation-kernel-on-a-gravitational-field-has-the-flat-leading-part-and-no-weyl-term-of-degree-four} argues. Under it, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products}(ii) gives that two extensions differ by derivatives of $\delta$ of order at most $2$, and Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-local-covariance-with-scaling-of-time-ordered-products}(iii) that for local covariant extensions with almost homogeneous scaling the difference is a local term in the sense of the statement; by (i) it is $\sum c_{i}K_{i}$. If both extensions are transverse in one slot, their difference $\Delta$ satisfies $\Delta(D\chi) = 0$ for every test scalar $\chi$ (transversality in the slot of $b$, integrated by parts onto $\chi$), on every field, and (ii) applies. The constants are those of the Fact, the same on every torsion-free field, so $c$ is the flat constant.

\emph{(iv) (argued).} The map $\chi \mapsto \bar\Pi(D\chi)$ vanishes off the diagonal when the unextended kernel is transverse there, so it is supported on the diagonal; that it is a polynomial in the curvature with constant coefficients and of dimension $3$ (one more than the kernel's local terms, from the extra derivative) is the supposition. The count as in (i): three derivatives on $\chi$ with one free vector slot, the invariants of four vector slots symmetrised give $D(D\cdot D\chi)$ up to lower order; one derivative on $\chi$ with $m^{2}$, $\mathcal{R}_{0}$ or the Ricci map; no derivative on $\chi$ with a vector of dimension $3$ built from the curvature, which is $D\mathcal{R}_{0}$ or the divergence of the Ricci map, equal to half of it by the contracted second Bianchi identity (classical, not stored); two derivatives with $m$ times an invariant of three vector slots, none. Subtracting $\sum_{i\geq 2}c_{i}K_{i}$ from $\bar\Pi$ changes the first four coefficients independently, by the rank computation of (ii). For the fifth, symmetry of the kernel makes $(\chi, \psi) \mapsto \int\psi\,D\cdot\bar\Pi(D\chi)$ symmetric; the first four terms are symmetric after integration by parts, and $\int\chi\,(D\mathcal{R}_{0})\cdot D\psi - \int\psi\,(D\mathcal{R}_{0})\cdot D\chi$ is not zero for $\psi = 1$ near the support of $\chi$ unless $\int\chi\,D\cdot D\mathcal{R}_{0} = 0$ for all $\chi$. This is an argument, not a proof: the supposition on the form of the divergence is the content of the literature's Ward identity on a gravitational field.
\end{proof}
